title: RICE-Delta: capacity-anchored token-economics prioritizer for latency-sensitive roadmaps
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Our current RICE variants score initiative value without explicitly modeling per-token cost deltas when we change model/quantization/batching and without tying that to latency elasticity under realistic capacity regimes. Goal: Produce a reproducible scoring extension (RICE-Delta) that augments Impact and Confidence with a token-cost delta and a latency-elasticity multiplier, and yields an actionable ranked list plus rollout gates (canary buckets + capacity shadow price).

Approach:
1) Base R, I, C, E (reach, impact, confidence, effort) remain. Add two terms: 
   - DeltaCost = predicted change in $/1000 tokens for target workload vs baseline (includes batching, KV cache hit-rate, quantization plan). Signed value: negative = cost savings.
   - LatencyElasticity = percentile-weighted sensitivity factor capturing how user-facing impact decays as median/95th latency shifts (derived from traffic shape and SLAs).
2) Final score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort + f(DeltaCost) * LatencyElasticityWeight, where f(DeltaCost) maps dollars saved into impact-equivalent points (anchored to historical A/B conversions).
3) Capacity shadow price: for Dedicated/Dedicated+Burst customers we compute marginal cost of additional reserved capacity and apply a penalty if initiative requires >X% new capacity during peak.
4) Scenario anchoring: run Monte Carlo across three traffic/capacity scenarios (Normal, Peak-Week, Degraded-Region) to return median and 90th percentile ranks.

Deliverables: scoring library (Python), a lightweight Confluence PRD, example scoring sheet for 12 candidate initiatives, simulation dashboards (Looker) and a rollout gating checklist that integrates with the Console's rollout feature.

Success metrics: relative stability vs baseline prioritization (>70% expected overlap for high-confidence items), measurable reduction in tokens/$ impact on top-10 items, and adoption by PMs for the next planning cycle.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Sofia: Kickoff meeting notes added. Agree to keep R/I/C/E canonical to preserve comparability with existing reports.
2026-03-05 - Ethan: Implemented initial DeltaCost estimator prototype using perf traces from runtime-1.18; early results show quantization yields ~18% cost delta for long-form summarization workload.
2026-03-06 - Marco Li (Eng): Requested we include KV cache hit-rate sensitivity; provided helper function outline in the PR link.
2026-03-09 - Product Review: PM council requested scenario anchoring (Normal/Peak/Degraded) and an easy visual that surfaces initiatives with high capacity penalties.
2026-03-12 - Design (Asha Patel): Suggested a 3-color badge system for Console UI: Green (no capacity penalty), Amber (moderate), Red (high). Working on mockups.

2026-03-14 - Ethan: Simulation dashboard uploaded. Ran 10k-sample Monte Carlo sweep; attached link to Looker. Next: translate DeltaCost to Impact-equivalents using conversion anchors from historical A/B (see reference link).
decision_notes: 2026-03-07 - Decision: Use a linear mapping from $/k token savings to Impact points, anchored such that $0.10/1k tokens saved == +0.5 Impact for workloads >100k QPS-equivalent tokens/month.
2026-03-10 - Decision: LatencyElasticity computed as 0.7*medianImpactDrop + 0.3*95thImpactDrop to prioritize user experience, per PM council vote.
2026-03-13 - Decision: Capacity shadow price implemented as an additive penalty on final score when projected peak reserved GPU-hours increase by >10% across Dedicated cluster.

2026-03-13 - Tradeoff: We will accept slightly higher effort estimates for initiatives that deliver >=12% token-cost reduction but require infra changes; these will be surfaced as 'infrastructure-heavy' buckets for engineering planning.
